$comment: Release manifest for candidate-5 (06-13-PLAN.md Task 2, 06-CONTEXT.md D-12/D-13).
Every value here is copied from a real continuous-integration run at the revision below.
Nothing in this file is measured locally. Where a lane has only local evidence, it is
recorded as BLOCKED with its reason, never as PASSED, because NOTHING LOCAL MAY BIND TO
LOCALLY BUILT BYTES (tooling/release-lanes.json).
THE PRODUCT CODE IS BYTE-IDENTICAL TO CANDIDATE-4'S AND CANDIDATE-3'S, and that is
measured rather than asserted: the package manifest's inputDigestSha256 is 713dd01d... at
all three revisions. Everything that changed is continuous-integration configuration and
planning documents. NOTHING under apps/ or packages/ moved.
SO WHY CUT IT. Because two lanes changed state, and neither changed because the software
improved. Both were passing all along and neither had a committed job that ran its own
declared command:
* quarterly-host-replacement PASSES for the first time. Candidates 1 through 4 blocked it
on credentials that belong to a DIFFERENT lane. It declares requiresSecrets FALSE and
needs nothing. This is the fourth lane in this project found in window 83.
* cross-adapter-phase PASSES for the first time, on a committed job, with legs_blocked=0
across electron, iphone, web-api and mcp against ONE server revision. This is SRV-02's
own stated closing command, and that box is restored in this candidate -- the first
requirement box this phase has closed on new continuous-integration evidence.
* 25 of 39 lanes PASS, against 23 at candidate-4, 22 at candidate-3, 14 at candidate-2,
11 at candidate-1.
A CORRECTION THIS CANDIDATE CARRIES. candidate-4's manifest said quarterly-host-replacement
was blocked partly on 'the DNS record name for the app host, and an SSH public key item'.
That was wrong, and it sent the owner after credentials that would have unblocked nothing.
Those inputs belong to live-host-dns-acceptance, which is sealed in code regardless of what
credentials exist. candidate-4 is NOT edited: it is the record of what was believed at its
own revision, and this entry is where the correction lives.
WHAT THIS CANDIDATE DOES NOT CLAIM:
* The passing drills say NOTHING about the backup credentials they demand or about any
real object store. That is .planning/WINDOWS.md row 100.
* desktop-e2e reported 0 flaky this run. Across FIVE runs of byte-identical code the
counts are 3, 1, 0, 1, 0. A clean run is one more sample of a nondeterministic suite,
NOT evidence the flake is fixed. Row 101 stays open.
* The build is still not reproducible, and the demonstration is now a series of three:
identical inputDigestSha256, three different applicationDigestSha256 values.
* DATA-03 and OPS-02 stay unchecked. They depend on live-host-dns-acceptance, which is
sealed by a deliberate line of code and owned by BACKLOG/999.2.
* 14 lanes are BLOCKED and each says why, with an owner.
This manifest is EXPECTED to verify non-zero. A non-zero verdict carrying stated reasons
is the honest outcome at this revision; a pass would require a release claim this
revision's evidence does not support.
Verify with:  node tooling/verify-release.mjs --manifest .planning/releases/candidate-5/release-manifest.json
Offline with: the same command plus --offline (degrades only the attestation step).
READ THE ATTESTATION LINE CAREFULLY. verify-release.mjs reports attestation=UNVERIFIED for
every artefact entry here, online and offline. That is NOT a statement that no attestation
exists -- one does, it verifies, and its decoded statement is retained under
evidence/attestation/. It is a statement that the committed entries are RECORDS of the
released bytes rather than the bytes, and the attestation is over the bytes. Closing that
gap is .planning/WINDOWS.md row 96.

THE ELECTRON LEG DRIVES DOWNLOADED BYTES, NOT LOCALLY BUILT ONES. The job needs desktop-package, downloads that artefact, re-verifies archiveDigestSha256 against the digest the build job recorded, and only then expands it with ditto. Packaging inside this job would have bound a cross-client proof to bytes it built itself, which tooling/release-lanes.json forbids outright.

THE iOS LEG NEEDS NO CREDENTIAL, which is a property of the repository rather than luck: apps/ios/Signing.xcconfig states that simulator builds need no team, so the job builds with CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO and installs to a booted simulator.

TWO ENVIRONMENT ASSUMPTIONS HAD TO BE FIXED FIRST, and both were invisible locally. apps/ios/Keepling.xcodeproj is gitignored and generated by XcodeGen, so a clean checkout had no project at all. And apps/ios/Package.swift declares swift-tools-version 6.3 while the macos-15 image's default Xcode ships Swift 6.1, so this job alone runs on macos-26 and asserts the floor -- reading the required version out of Package.swift itself -- immediately after checkout.

ONE PART OF SRV-02's STATED CLOSING COMMAND IS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, and it is not an oversight. That disclosure also says to add the lane to requiredLanes in tooling/check-ci-contract.mjs. That list is asserted EQUAL to `tooling/test-phase-2.sh --list`; adding a lane that is not a Phase 2 lane would break the inventory check the list exists to enforce. The intent -- that the lane cannot be skipped without something failing -- is met instead by desktop-promote's needs, which now include this job.
